channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: How LeBron James Scored $300 Million From Insurers
item.description: When LeBron James signed up to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to NBA glory with a $154 million contract in 2018, it wasn’t the biggest deal he did that year. His limited liability company borrowed almost $300 million from two Midwestern life insurers, Sridhar Natarajan explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Conference Board CEO: Consumers Worried About the Future
item.description: Steve Odland, CEO of The Conference Board, discussed the recent consumer confidence data showing a significant divergence between current sentiment and future expectations. The present situation index increased by 6.8 points, reflecting consumers' relatively positive feelings due to full employment and rising wages. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Mormon Church Is Putting Its Real Estate Empire to Work
item.description: After decades of quietly amassing billions of dollars in land, the institution is investing in more deals and planning massive projects that stand to reshape communities. Bloomberg's Natalie Wong, Ann Choi and Katie Meyer explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EchoStar Deals Worth $1.5 Billion Must be Investigated, US Says
item.description: EchoStar Corp. allegedly engaged in $1.5 billion of “unusual transactions” with its bankrupt subsidiary, Hughes Satellite Systems Corp., according to the US Trustee, who urged the court to appoint an examiner to investigate the deals.
item.dc:creator: Steven Church

item.title: Intuit Sinks 11% on Weak Outlook as Nvidia Earnings Loom | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Norah Mulinda and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Consumers Are Signaling an Uneven Economy, Abby Joseph Cohen Says
item.description: Abby Joseph Cohen, Columbia Business School professor and former partner at Goldman Sachs, says recent consumer spending patterns are signaling issues with the US economy. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," she also warns AI investing may not be sustainable and previews the Jackson Hole Federal Reserve meeting. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US-Canada Cosmetic Tariffs Threaten the $10 Beauty Impulse Buy
item.description: In between offering advice on how to find the best towels and where to buy affordable versions of high-end garments, Bryce Gruber recently waded into the US-Canada trade war, warning her social-media followers that some of their favorite makeup is about to get more expensive.
item.dc:creator: Christine Dobby and Mathieu Dion

item.title: Congress Will Have to Act to Address $40T US Debt, Says Fmr. Rep. Kevin Brady
item.description: Kevin Brady, former Republican Congressman from Texas, said that the US is failing to restrain spending, even as the US brings in record revenues. Brady said that congress will have to act to reduce spending, including looking at programs like Social Security and Medicaid that are moving towards insolvency issues. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Braskem’s $11 Billion Debt Rework Puts Spotlight on Petrobras
item.description: Braskem SA’s announcement of an $11 billion debt restructuring staved off an immediate crisis that would have pushed it into bankruptcy protection. But the parties remain far apart on key issues ranging from terms of shareholder support to how existing debt will be reworked.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Gamarski, Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo and Cristiane Lucchesi

item.title: Binance Hires Two Senior Compliance Executives From Crypto.com
item.description: Binance Holdings Ltd. has hired two senior compliance executives from Crypto.com as the exchange bolsters ranks in that department after a number of staff departures and ongoing regulatory scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Ben Weiss

item.title: Short Squeeze in US Long Bonds Shows ‘Bessent Put’ at Work
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s surprise plan to tamp down US borrowing costs by expanding bond buybacks may have sparked fierce debate about its ultimate effectiveness, but key market metrics and positioning show that it’s having an impact.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Elizabeth Stanton

item.title: Guggenheim Investments Says Affiliates May Buy Its Hard-Hit Loan
item.description: Guggenheim Investments, the asset-management arm of Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners, is telling lenders that affiliates may look to buy portions of a loan issued by its financing entity after the debt’s value collapsed in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Basu

item.title: New Iran Sanctions Part of 'Piecemeal Strategy,' Says Rep. Gabe Amo
item.description: Representative Gabe Amo, a Rhode Island Democrat, called the US threat of sanctions against countries doing business with Iran more of the president's "piecemeal strategy" that's leaving the administration "grasping at straws." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: United Airlines CEO on Expansion Plans, Airfares, Demand
item.description: United Airlines Chief Executive Officer Scott Kirby discusses the largest international expansion in the company’s history, the strength he sees in both customer demand and the US economy, and plans to offset increased oil prices. The carrier will now fly to 10 more destinations in Europe and Asia. Kirby speaks to Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz from United's hub at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Natural Gas Falls as Iran Pressure Plan Pulls Down Energy
item.description: US natural gas futures ended lower, but pared back most losses, after earlier being pulled down by crude and European gas futures. Those global energy prices fell on a US plan to increase economic pressure on Iran that seemed less likely to affect physical supply than investors expected.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: Treasuries Gain as Oil Drop Eases Pressure on Inflation, Bessent
item.description: Treasuries gained as a decline in crude-oil prices eased inflation concerns and pressure on Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has been trying to halt a months-long selloff that pushed the longest-dated yields to the highest in almost two decades.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie

item.title: Gold Edges Up After Four-Day Gain as Traders Eye Treasury Moves
item.description: Gold edged higher as inflation concerns eased, extending a four-day rally sparked by a surprise bond-market intervention that’s revived concerns over US fiscal policy and dollar weakness.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie and Sybilla Gross

item.title: Stocks Rise Before Nvidia as Oil Drop Lifts Bonds: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks rose as a decline in oil prices sent bond yields lower, with traders awaiting Nvidia Corp.’s earnings for clues on whether the outlook for artificial intelligence remains intact.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Oil Falls on Fresh Iran War Diplomacy, Talks on Hormuz
item.description: Oil extended declines as fresh diplomatic efforts helped renew optimism the Iran war would not escalate, while a US plan to ramp up economic pressure on Tehran spared the country’s trading partners from harsher measures for now.
item.dc:creator: Charles Gorrivan, Alex Longley and Nicholas Lua

item.title: Copy Trading Offers Alternative to Traditional Investing
item.description: Steven Wang, Founder & CEO of Dub, launched the copy trading platform 3 years ago after dropping out of Harvard to become an entrepreneur. He says the app offers a unique alternative to sports betting, and fresh opportunities for the increasing number of young Americans who say they are now investing their money to grow try and grow their wealth. Wang says Dub is for great traders who "don't need to go the traditional sort of boys club and Wall Street path to really become the next superstar." (Source: Bloomberg)
